newsitem.title: USA: Port Auth of NY-NJ plans bond sale for April 21.
newsitem.headline: Port Auth of NY-NJ plans bond sale for April 21.

text.p: The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey plans to sell $920 million of revenue bonds during the week of April 21, said an official at one of the co-senior underwriters, Lehman Brothers.

The bonds will pay for a new international arrivals building at John F. Kennedy Airport in the Queens Borough of New York City. The Port Authority last week said the deal might be delayed a couple of weeks or so due to the complexity of the contract with the developer, but added it definitely would occur before the end of April.
"That's the current schedule, the week of April 21," said the Lehman Brothers official, who declined to be named.
He added the syndicate was exploring whether or not it would prove sufficiently cost-effective to buy bond insurance for some of the debt, which would open up the sale to retail investors.
"Nothing's come up to say we won't. I feel pretty good about getting it," he replied, when asked about the likelihood of insuring some of the bonds.
